concept.title: NC State Cybersecurity Guide
concept.shortdesc: Essential cybersecurity concepts, step-by-step setup guides, and campus resources for NC State students, faculty, and staff.

conbody.p: Welcome to the NC State Cybersecurity Guide. This documentation provides NC State students, faculty, and staff with practical guidance, campus-specific instructions, and reference resources to protect Unity accounts, personal devices, and university data.

ul.li: Students: Learn how to set up Duo two-factor authentication, manage passwords, stay safe on public Wi-Fi, connect to the NC State VPN from off campus, and recognize campus scams.
Faculty and Staff: Access instructions for securing university-managed devices, following institutional password and data security guidelines, and reporting cybersecurity incidents.

Two-Factor Authentication (2FA): Explains how multifactor authentication reduces account compromise and provides step-by-step instructions for enrolling in Duo, adding new devices or phones, and using bypass codes.
Password Management: Covers how to create strong, unique passwords, use password managers, follow NC State password guidelines, and change your Unity ID password.

Virtual Private Network (VPN): Explains how encrypted VPN connections protect remote traffic and provides instructions for installing Cisco Secure Client, connecting to the NC State VPN, and authenticating with Duo.
Phishing: Identifies common phishing tactics and NC State campus scams, explains how to spot suspicious messages, and outlines how to report phishing emails through Gmail and the OIT Help Desk.
Ransomware: Defines ransomware and common attack types, explains how to analyze suspicious emails that deliver malware, and lists ransomware protection software and awareness resources.
Data Breach: Explains what data breaches are, how to recognize suspicious breach notifications, examples of higher education data breaches, and NC State campus data security training guidelines.
Incident Response: Covers types of cybersecurity incidents, official response protocols and technologies, and how to report a cybersecurity incident on campus.
Alert Fatigue: Explains the causes and effects of alert fatigue and provides instructions for opting into high-priority campus security alerts and organizing incoming emails with Google filters.
Network Security: Introduces network security concepts and best practices for protecting your devices and data when using public Wi-Fi networks.
Outdated Software: Explains the security risks of outdated software, provides steps for updating macOS and Windows operating systems, and links to NC State IT Service Portal update guides.
Cookies: Explains what browser cookies are, how different types of cookies work, and how to clear cookies and cache across web browsers.
Autofill Information: Covers autofill security risks and best practices, along with instructions for accessing, changing, and deleting saved autofill information.
